metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider B2's 'derive its own plan-review analog': prefer refactoring _opcert_anchor_event (verify_opcert.py:58) to take a `kind` argument (defaulting to completion-verifier) and calling it with the plan-review kind, so both anchor resolvers share one implementation of the story-4214 storage-anchor scan.
evidence: verify_opcert.py:79: `if attestation_kind(data.get('manifest'), data) != KIND: continue` — KIND is a module constant (line 33), the ONLY kind-specific line in the scan
verify_opcert.py:58-82: the rest of _opcert_anchor_event (filename-order walk, `data.get('envelope')` filter, terminal-anchor selection, None-on-absence fail-closed) is kind-agnostic
The scan encodes the story-4214/Option-B storage-anchor contract; two copies can drift
findings.finding: B2's anchor derivation duplicates the load-bearing terminal-SIGNATURE anchor scan (verify_opcert.py:58-82 _opcert_anchor_event) rather than parameterizing the existing resolver by kind; the plan says B2 'derives its own plan-review analog' because that resolver is 'hardcoded to the completion-verifier kind'. The only difference between the two is the KIND filter at line 79 (attestation_kind(...) != KIND); the surrounding scan (filename-order walk, envelope-bearing filter, terminal-event selection, fail-closed-on-None) is identical and security-critical. Duplicating it risks the two anchor resolvers drifting under future changes (e.g. the story-4214 storage-anchor rule).
findings.location: Approach section, B2: 'the CLI's _opcert_anchor_event resolver is hardcoded to the completion-verifier kind, so B2 derives its own plan-review analog'
scenarios: A future change to the storage-anchor selection rule updates the completion-verifier resolver but not B2's copy (or vice versa), silently diverging the plan-review era-validity anchor from the completion-verifier one
findings.suggested_fix: Parameterize `_opcert_anchor_event(events, ticket_id, kind=KIND)` and have B2 pass the plan-review kind, keeping the single terminal-SIGNATURE anchor scan authoritative for both attestation kinds rather than maintaining a second copy.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign the leaf to a subset of its declared parent (epic 6982's plan-review-gate contract): either scope B2's Gerrit code-review criterion, scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py, and the rebar-debug Phase-1-exit hook under a parent whose plan contains them (or update the epic to admit them, restaling its plan-review attestation), or reparent this leaf so its declared parent actually contains the code-review/Gerrit + debug-skill work.
evidence: Parent 6982 Context: 'Integrate the task-decomposition SOTA research ... into the plan-review gate'; 'Implementation targets: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/ (orchestrator, det_floor.py, passes.py, criteria_routing.json), src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/ ..., src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_*.md.'
Parent 6982 deliverables are R1-R7 plan-review-gate criteria/instrumentation + experiments E1/E2/E3/E5/E6 — no Gerrit merge-gate code-review criterion, no backtest script, no rebar-debug skill hook.
Leaf B2: 'DET code-review criterion at Gerrit' running in the 'review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)' — a code-review/merge-gate subsystem distinct from the plan-review gate the epic scopes.
Leaf Scope: 'rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook: ... coordinate with the debug-skill child 78f1' — a rebar-debug skill deliverable outside epic 6982's plan-review-gate contract.
Leaf AC: 'scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py (one-shot, committed with the change)' — not part of the epic's experiment set (all E-experiments closed/rescoped).
The sibling R4 story 03a9 (also a child of 6982) shipped the light bug tier B1 extends; 03a9 is a sibling, not this leaf's parent, so it does not supply containment for B2/backtest/debug-hook.
findings.finding: The leaf delivers three deliverables that its declared parent (epic 6982) does not contain: (1) B2's Gerrit merge-gate DET code-review criterion in the review-bot VOTE pipeline, (2) the committed one-shot backtest script scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py, and (3) the rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook sentence. Epic 6982's contract is explicitly scoped to the PLAN-REVIEW GATE (R1-R7 recommendations; targets src/rebar/llm/plan_review/, review_kernel, reviewers/plan_review_*.md; experiments E1/E2/E3/E5/E6). A code-review/Gerrit merge-gate criterion, a corpus backtest, and a debug-skill hook are in different subsystems the epic's plan does not enumerate — the leaf steps outside the parent's contract.
findings.location: Plan Approach B2 + Scope ('review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)', 'rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook') + Acceptance Criteria (Gerrit DET criterion; backtest property; debug-skill hook); parent epic 6982 Context/Scope.
scenarios: A reviewer or the epic owner treats epic 6982's closed plan-review-gate contract as authoritative and finds the leaf shipping code-review/Gerrit and debug-skill work the epic never scoped.
The completion-verifier or merge gate audits leaf-vs-parent scope and flags divergence for the out-of-subsystem deliverables.

findings.finding: B1's escalation mechanism enables blocking (lifts the forced det_blocking=[]) but does not itself produce blocking findings; det_floor.det_blocking_findings only returns findings when a DET rule actually blocked. The AC/testing assertion 'precheck det_blocking non-empty' therefore only holds if the test fixture deliberately trips a DET rule, conflating 'blocking enabled' with 'a block fired'.
findings.location: Testing section ('precheck det_blocking non-empty AND route_criteria returns the full set') and AC line 1 ('precheck det_blocking')

findings.finding: B2's cross-host verify chain names opcert_from_record→trusted_env_keyring→verify_opcert but omits verify_opcert's mandatory storage_anchor_commit/position input, which is NOT a signed/bound field and whose only resolver is CLI-local and hardcoded to the completion-verifier kind — so the plan-review verification surface is only partially specified.
findings.location: Approach §B2 ('read the ticket's plan-review SIGNATURE record ... verify with attest.opcert.verify_opcert (kind-bound, storage-anchor era rule)'); AC3
findings.suggested_fix: Add a read-only helper (beside the B2 criterion or reused from verify_opcert.py) that walks the merged log for the terminal envelope-bearing SIGNATURE event whose derived attestation_kind == plan-review, resolves its introducing tickets-branch commit + position via build_introducing_commit_map/resolve_event_commit, and passes (storage_anchor_commit, storage_anchor_position, merged_log_commit from the bound fields, recomputed material_fingerprint) into verify_opcert with principal=record principal and kind=plan-review. Classify an unresolvable anchor as INFRA/unavailable (fail-open advisory), not FLAG.

findings.finding: B2's cross-host verification protocol omits the storage-anchor inputs that verify_opcert requires; the derivation the plan enumerates cannot actually call verify_opcert.
findings.location: Approach B2 ('read the ticket's plan-review SIGNATURE record ... decode via opcert_from_record ... verify with attest.opcert.verify_opcert'); AC #3
findings.suggested_fix: State that B2 derives the storage anchor from the ticket's terminal plan-review SIGNATURE event using the same _opcert_anchor_event/_resolve_commit machinery (adapted to KIND=plan-review) that verify_opcert.py composes, failing OPEN/advisory (not FLAG) when the anchor is unresolvable; and specify that the keyring principal is the project-required/pinned environment (as verify_required_environment does) rather than the record's self-claimed principal, or justify the weaker record-principal trust model explicitly.

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'the symmetric HMAC scheme is retired — signing.py header', but the named source (src/rebar/signing.py header, lines 3-6) states the opposite for reads: legacy HMAC attestations REMAIN VERIFIABLE ('reads dispatch by record shape so legacy HMAC attestations remain verifiable'); only new WRITES mint op-certs. The 'retired' framing is an overstatement of the cited header.
findings.location: Approach, B2: '(the symmetric HMAC scheme is retired — signing.py header)'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace '(the symmetric HMAC scheme is retired — signing.py header)' with '(new writes mint rebar.opcert.v1 op-certs; legacy HMAC records remain readable but carry no decodable envelope — signing.py header)'.
